ramayana-2-1-1.translation: After some time, King Dasharatha, joy of the Raghus, spoke to his son Bharata, son of Kaikeyi.
ramayana-2-1-1.meaning: The second book opens with Dasharatha speaking to Bharata.
ramayana-2-1-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-2.translation: This son of the Kekaya king, your uncle Yudhajit, is staying here, my son; he has come to take you with him, hero.
ramayana-2-1-2.meaning: Bharata's uncle wants to take him home.
ramayana-2-1-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-3.translation: Hearing this from Dasharatha, Bharata son of Kaikeyi prepared to go, together with Shatrughna.
ramayana-2-1-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-4.translation: Taking leave of his father, of Rama who acted without strain, and of his mothers, the best of men went with Shatrughna.
ramayana-2-1-4.meaning: They say goodbye to the family.
ramayana-2-1-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-5.translation: Yudhajit, delighted to have Bharata and Shatrughna, entered his own city, and his father was pleased.
ramayana-2-1-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-6.translation: Bharata lived there with his brother, honoured with hospitality and cherished by his uncle Ashvapati with a father's love.
ramayana-2-1-6.meaning: Bharata is loved in his mother's home.
ramayana-2-1-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-7.translation: Though living there, satisfied in every wish, the two heroic brothers remembered their old father, King Dasharatha.
ramayana-2-1-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-8.translation: The mighty king too remembered his two absent sons, Bharata and Shatrughna, like great Indra and Varuna.
ramayana-2-1-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-9.translation: All four bulls among men were dear to him, like four arms grown from his own body.
ramayana-2-1-9.meaning: He loved all four sons as part of himself.
ramayana-2-1-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-10.translation: Of them, mighty Rama gave his father the most joy; like Brahma among beings, he was the most virtuous.
ramayana-2-1-10.meaning: Rama was his father's special delight.
ramayana-2-1-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-11.translation: With Bharata gone, Rama and mighty Lakshmana honoured their god-like father.
ramayana-2-1-11.meaning: The two brothers serve their father.
ramayana-2-1-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-12.translation: Placing his father's command first, righteous Rama carried out all the city's affairs, pleasing and beneficial.
ramayana-2-1-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-13.translation: Taking great care, he did what was due to his mothers and attended to his elders' needs at the proper times.
ramayana-2-1-13.meaning: He is attentive to every family member.
ramayana-2-1-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-14.translation: So Dasharatha was pleased, and so were the brahmins, the merchants and all who lived in the land, by Rama's conduct and character.
ramayana-2-1-14.meaning: Everyone is happy with Rama's character.
ramayana-2-1-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-15.translation: He was always calm and spoke gently first; even when spoken to harshly he did not answer back.
ramayana-2-1-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-16.translation: He was pleased by even a single kindness done to him, and, being self-possessed, did not remember even a hundred wrongs.
ramayana-2-1-16.meaning: He remembered kindness and forgot injuries.
ramayana-2-1-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-17.translation: Even between his weapons practice he always sat talking with good people, elders in character, wisdom and age.
ramayana-2-1-17.meaning: He sought the company of the wise.
ramayana-2-1-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-18.translation: He was of noble birth, good, never downcast, truthful and straightforward, trained by elders and by brahmins who saw dharma and purpose.
ramayana-2-1-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-19.translation: He knew the truth of dharma, wealth and pleasure; he had a sharp memory and quick insight, and was skilled and practised in worldly custom.
ramayana-2-1-19.meaning: He was wise in every part of life.
ramayana-2-1-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-20.translation: He knew the scriptures, was grateful, understood people, and was wise in when to restrain and when to favour, as was just.
ramayana-2-1-20.meaning: He was a fair judge of character.
ramayana-2-1-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-21.translation: He knew the means of raising revenue and understood spending; he excelled in all the branches of learning, even the mixed ones.
ramayana-2-1-21.meaning: He was skilled in finance and learning.
ramayana-2-1-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-22.translation: Balancing wealth and dharma, he enjoyed pleasure but was never lazy; he understood the arts of recreation and how to divide resources.
ramayana-2-1-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-23.translation: He was skilled in riding and training elephants and horses, the best of those who knew archery, honoured in the world as a master chariot-warrior.
ramayana-2-1-23.meaning: He was a superb horseman and archer.
ramayana-2-1-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-24.translation: He could lead an attack and strike, was skilled in leading armies, and could not be overcome in battle even by angry gods and demons.
ramayana-2-1-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-25.translation: He was free of envy, had conquered anger, was neither proud nor jealous, despised no living being, and was not ruled by time.
ramayana-2-1-25.meaning: Inner qualities: no envy, anger or pride.
ramayana-2-1-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-26.translation: Thus endowed with the best qualities, the prince was loved by his people and honoured in the three worlds; like the earth in patience, like Brihaspati in wisdom, like Indra in valour.
ramayana-2-1-26.meaning: Rama combined patience, wisdom and courage.
ramayana-2-1-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-27.translation: With these qualities, loved by all the people and bringing his father joy, Rama shone like the blazing sun with its rays.
ramayana-2-1-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-28.translation: The earth itself longed for him as its lord, so perfect in conduct, of irresistible valour, like a guardian of the world.
ramayana-2-1-28.meaning: The whole land wanted him as king.
ramayana-2-1-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-29.translation: Seeing his son endowed with so many matchless qualities, King Dasharatha, scorcher of foes, began to think.
ramayana-2-1-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-30.translation: This was the dearest wish turning in his heart: When will I see my dear son crowned?
ramayana-2-1-30.meaning: His heart's wish was to see Rama crowned.
ramayana-2-1-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-31.translation: He wishes the world to prosper and has compassion for all beings; he is dearer to the people than I am, like a rain cloud.
ramayana-2-1-31.meaning: Rama is loved even more than the king.
ramayana-2-1-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-32.translation: He is equal to Yama and Indra in valour, to Brihaspati in judgment, to a mountain in steadiness, and more virtuous than I.
ramayana-2-1-32.meaning: Dasharatha admits his son surpasses him.
ramayana-2-1-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-33.translation: May I, at this age, see my son ruling this whole earth, and so attain heaven.
ramayana-2-1-33.meaning: He wishes to see Rama rule before he dies.
ramayana-2-1-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-34.translation: Seeing him endowed with every rising virtue, the great king decided with his ministers to make him crown prince.
ramayana-2-1-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-35.translation: The lord of the earth summoned the leading men of the land, from many cities and from the countryside.
ramayana-2-1-35.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-36.translation: Seated on the various seats the king had given them, the kings sat facing him, composed.
ramayana-2-1-36.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-1-37.translation: Surrounded by honoured, courteous kings and people of town and country seated around him, the king shone like thousand-eyed Indra among the gods.
ramayana-2-1-37.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 1: Bharata leaves to visit his uncle in Kekaya. Rama's goodness, skill and gentle character are described at length, and Dasharatha, growing old, decides to make him crown prince.

ramayana-2-2-1.translation: Then, addressing the whole assembly, the lord of the earth spoke these matchless words, beneficial and uplifting.
ramayana-2-2-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-2.translation: In a great deep, echoing voice like the sound of a drum, the king spoke, thundering like a cloud.
ramayana-2-2-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-3.translation: I wish to bring good fortune to this whole world, protected by my ancestors, the Ikshvaku kings, and worthy of happiness.
ramayana-2-2-3.meaning: He states his aim: the people's welfare.
ramayana-2-2-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-4.translation: I too have followed the path of my forebears, always tirelessly protecting the people as best I could.
ramayana-2-2-4.meaning: He has ruled as his ancestors did.
ramayana-2-2-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-5.translation: Working for the good of the whole world, I have grown old in this body under the shade of the white royal umbrella.
ramayana-2-2-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-6.translation: Having lived a long life of many thousands of years, I wish to rest this worn-out body.
ramayana-2-2-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-7.translation: I am worn out carrying the heavy burden of dharma for the world, which comes with royal power and is hard to bear for those who have not mastered their senses.
ramayana-2-2-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-8.translation: I wish to rest by placing my son in charge of the people's welfare, with the consent of all these brahmins gathered here.
ramayana-2-2-8.meaning: He proposes handing over to his son.
ramayana-2-2-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-9.translation: My eldest son Rama, conqueror of enemy cities, equal to Indra in valour, has inherited all my virtues.
ramayana-2-2-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-10.translation: Gladly I will install that bull among men, best of upholders of dharma, as crown prince, as the moon is joined with the star Pushya.
ramayana-2-2-10.meaning: He will make Rama crown prince at an auspicious time.
ramayana-2-2-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-11.translation: Lakshmana's elder brother, blessed with fortune, will be a fitting lord for you; with him as lord even the three worlds would be well protected.
ramayana-2-2-11.meaning: Rama would be a worthy ruler.
ramayana-2-2-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-12.translation: Joining this land with this good fortune, and placing it in my son's care, I will be free of strain.
ramayana-2-2-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-13.translation: As he spoke, the kings joyfully welcomed the king, like peacocks greeting a great, thundering rain cloud.
ramayana-2-2-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-14.translation: Understanding fully the intent of the king who knew dharma and purpose, they considered it in their minds and spoke to old King Dasharatha.
ramayana-2-2-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-15.translation: You are old, O king, of many thousands of years. Crown Rama as crown prince.
ramayana-2-2-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-16.translation: Hearing these words so pleasing to him, the king, as if he did not know, said this, wanting to test them:
ramayana-2-2-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-17.translation: Why, while I rule the earth with dharma, do you want to see my son as crown prince?
ramayana-2-2-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-18.translation: They and the people of town and country said to the great king: Your son has many fine qualities, O king.
ramayana-2-2-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-19.translation: With divine virtues, Rama, true in valour, equal to Indra, surpasses all the Ikshvakus, lord of people.
ramayana-2-2-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-20.translation: Rama is a good man in the world, devoted to truth and dharma, knowing dharma, true to his word, of good character, free of envy.
ramayana-2-2-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-21.translation: He is patient, comforting, gentle, grateful, master of his senses, soft-spoken and steady-minded, always kind and without envy.
ramayana-2-2-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-22.translation: Raghava speaks kindly and truthfully to all beings, and attends upon learned, elderly brahmins.
ramayana-2-2-22.meaning: Kind speech and respect for elders.
ramayana-2-2-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-23.translation: So his matchless fame, glory and power grow here; he is skilled in all the weapons of gods, demons and men.
ramayana-2-2-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-24.translation: When he goes to battle for a village or city with Saumitri, he never returns without victory.
ramayana-2-2-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-25.translation: Returning from battle on elephant or chariot, he always asks the citizens about their welfare as if they were his own family.
ramayana-2-2-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-26.translation: About their sons, sacred fires, wives, servants and pupils, fully and in order, as a father asks about his own sons,
ramayana-2-2-26.meaning: He asks about every part of their lives.
ramayana-2-2-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-27.translation: Do your pupils serve you, and are they diligent in their work? This is what that tiger among men, Rama, always asks us.
ramayana-2-2-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-28.translation: He is deeply grieved at people's troubles and rejoices like a father in all their festivals.
ramayana-2-2-28.meaning: He shares their sorrows and joys.
ramayana-2-2-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-29.translation: Truthful, a great archer, serving his elders, master of his senses: this child has been born for your good fortune; happily he is your Raghava, endowed with a son's virtues, as Kashyapa was to Marichi.
ramayana-2-2-29.meaning: Rama is a blessing to his father.
ramayana-2-2-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-30.translation: All the people in the kingdom and in the capital wish strength, health and long life to self-knowing Rama.
ramayana-2-2-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-31.translation: People inside and outside the city, of town and country, women old and young, morning and evening with focused minds,
ramayana-2-2-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-32.translation: bow to all the gods for the sake of famous Rama. May their prayers be fulfilled by your grace, lord.
ramayana-2-2-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-33.translation: We wish to see Rama, dark as a blue lotus, destroyer of all enemies, your son, best of kings, established as crown prince.
ramayana-2-2-33.meaning: They want to see him crowned.
ramayana-2-2-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-2-34.translation: Your god-like son, devoted to the good of the whole world, you should quickly and joyfully crown for our good, giver of boons.
ramayana-2-2-34.meaning: They urge the king to act.
ramayana-2-2-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 2: Dasharatha tells the assembly he wishes to retire and install Rama as crown prince. The people joyfully agree and list Rama's virtues.

ramayana-2-3-1.translation: Accepting their lotus-like folded hands raised on all sides, the king spoke to them pleasing and beneficial words.
ramayana-2-3-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-2.translation: Ah, I am delighted, and my influence is boundless, since you want my dear eldest son as crown prince.
ramayana-2-3-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-3.translation: Having honoured them, the king said this to the brahmins Vasishtha and Vamadeva as the others listened:
ramayana-2-3-3.meaning: He gives orders to the priests.
ramayana-2-3-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-4.translation: This glorious month of Chaitra is holy, its forests in flower. Let everything be prepared for Rama's installation as crown prince.
ramayana-2-3-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-5.translation: The two best of brahmins came to the lord of the world and, glad and joyful, said: It is done as you say.
ramayana-2-3-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-6.translation: Then the radiant king said to Sumantra: Bring self-possessed Rama here quickly.
ramayana-2-3-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-7.translation: Sumantra agreed and, at the king's command, brought Rama, best of chariot-warriors, there by chariot.
ramayana-2-3-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-8.translation: Then the kings seated there around King Dasharatha, from the east, north, west and south,
ramayana-2-3-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-9.translation: mlecchas and aryas and others who lived in the forests and mountains, all attended him like the gods around Indra.
ramayana-2-3-9.meaning: People of every land and culture.
ramayana-2-3-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-10.translation: Among them the royal sage, like Indra among the Maruts, from his palace saw his son coming in a chariot.
ramayana-2-3-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-11.translation: Like a king of the gandharvas, famed for his manliness, long-armed, great-hearted, walking like a proud elephant,
ramayana-2-3-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-12.translation: with a face lovely as the moon, most pleasing to see, stealing the eyes and hearts of men with his beauty, generosity and virtues,
ramayana-2-3-12.meaning: He captivates all who see him.
ramayana-2-3-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-13.translation: like a rain cloud cheering people scorched by summer heat: the king could not have enough of watching him approach.
ramayana-2-3-13.meaning: His father gazes at him with delight.
ramayana-2-3-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-14.translation: Sumantra helped Raghava down from the fine chariot and followed behind with folded hands as he went to his father.
ramayana-2-3-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-15.translation: The best of men, Raghava, climbed the palace, shining like a peak of Kailasa, with the charioteer, to see the king.
ramayana-2-3-15.meaning: He goes up to the hall.
ramayana-2-3-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-16.translation: Approaching with folded hands and bowing near his father, Rama announced his name and touched his father's feet.
ramayana-2-3-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-17.translation: Seeing him bowed at his side with folded hands, the king took his hands, drew him close and embraced his dear son.
ramayana-2-3-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-18.translation: The glorious king pointed Rama to a splendid seat set ready for him, adorned with gems and gold.
ramayana-2-3-18.meaning: He offers Rama a place of honour.
ramayana-2-3-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-19.translation: Taking that fine seat, Raghava lit it up with his own radiance, like the clear rising sun lighting Mount Meru.
ramayana-2-3-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha orders preparations for Rama's installation in the spring month of Chaitra and summons Rama to the palace.

ramayana-2-3-20.translation: Lit up by him, the hall shone like the clear autumn sky with its planets and stars lit by the moon.
ramayana-2-3-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-21.translation: Looking at his dear son, the king was delighted, as if seeing himself adorned in a mirror.
ramayana-2-3-21.meaning: He sees himself in his son.
ramayana-2-3-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-22.translation: Smiling, the best of fathers spoke to his son, as Kashyapa spoke to Indra:
ramayana-2-3-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-23.translation: You are my worthy son, born of my worthy eldest queen, best in virtues, my dear son Rama.
ramayana-2-3-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-24.translation: Since the people are devoted to you through your virtues, become crown prince under the star Pushya.
ramayana-2-3-24.meaning: The people's love earns him the role.
ramayana-2-3-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-25.translation: By nature you are disciplined and virtuous; yet out of love, son, I will tell you what is good for you, though you are virtuous.
ramayana-2-3-25.meaning: Even good people benefit from loving advice.
ramayana-2-3-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-26.translation: Be even more humble and always master your senses. Give up the vices that come from desire and anger.
ramayana-2-3-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-27.translation: Through what you do both openly and unseen, keep your ministers and all your subjects content.
ramayana-2-3-27.meaning: Earn people's trust in public and in private.
ramayana-2-3-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-28.translation: When a king protects the earth with contented, loyal subjects, his friends rejoice like the gods on gaining nectar. So, son, act always with self-restraint.
ramayana-2-3-28.meaning: Happy people make a strong kingdom.
ramayana-2-3-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-29.translation: Hearing this, Rama's friends, eager to please him, hurried to tell Kausalya.
ramayana-2-3-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-30.translation: Kausalya, finest of women, ordered gold, cows and many jewels to be given to those who brought the good news.
ramayana-2-3-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-31.translation: Then, bowing to the king, Raghava mounted his chariot and went to his own bright palace, honoured by crowds.
ramayana-2-3-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-3-32.translation: And the citizens, hearing the king's words as if they had gained a cherished wish, took leave of the king, went home and joyfully worshipped the gods.
ramayana-2-3-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 3: Dasharatha tells Rama he will be crown prince and gives him fatherly advice on ruling with self-control. Kausalya rejoices.

ramayana-2-4-1.translation: When the citizens had gone, the king again took counsel with his ministers and, knowing how to decide, made his decision.
ramayana-2-4-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-2.translation: Tomorrow will be Pushya; tomorrow let my son Rama, with eyes like red lotuses, be crowned crown prince, the lord decided.
ramayana-2-4-2.meaning: He fixes the coronation for the next day.
ramayana-2-4-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-3.translation: Then, entering the inner palace, King Dasharatha ordered the charioteer: Bring Rama here again.
ramayana-2-4-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-4.translation: Accepting the order, the charioteer quickly went again to Rama's house to bring him.
ramayana-2-4-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-5.translation: Hearing from the doorkeepers that he had come again, Rama grew uneasy.
ramayana-2-4-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-6.translation: Admitting him quickly, Rama said: Tell me fully why you have come again.
ramayana-2-4-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-7.translation: The charioteer said: The king wishes to see you. Having heard, decide whether to go or not.
ramayana-2-4-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-8.translation: Hearing the charioteer, Rama hurried to the royal palace to see the king again.
ramayana-2-4-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-9.translation: Hearing Rama had arrived, King Dasharatha had him brought in, wishing to tell him dear news.
ramayana-2-4-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-10.translation: As soon as glorious Raghava entered his father's palace, he saw his father from afar and bowed down with folded hands.
ramayana-2-4-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-11.translation: Raising him up as he bowed and embracing him, the king showed him a fine seat and spoke again.
ramayana-2-4-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-12.translation: Rama, I am old and long-lived; I have enjoyed the pleasures I wanted and performed hundreds of sacrifices rich in food and gifts.
ramayana-2-4-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-13.translation: The child I longed for was born, you, matchless on earth today. I have given, sacrificed and studied, best of men.
ramayana-2-4-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-14.translation: I have known the joys I wanted, hero; I am free of debt to gods, sages, ancestors, brahmins and myself.
ramayana-2-4-14.meaning: He has paid all life's debts.
ramayana-2-4-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-15.translation: Nothing remains for me to do except your coronation. So you should do what I tell you.
ramayana-2-4-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-16.translation: Today all the people want you as their ruler. So I will crown you crown prince, my son.
ramayana-2-4-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-17.translation: Also, Rama, I am seeing terrible, ill-omened dreams; great meteors are falling here with thunder and roaring.
ramayana-2-4-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-18.translation: Astrologers tell me, Rama, that my birth star is beset by fierce planets: the sun, Mars and Rahu.
ramayana-2-4-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-19.translation: When such omens appear, usually a king dies or meets terrible misfortune.
ramayana-2-4-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-20.translation: So, while my mind is still clear, Raghava, be crowned, for people's minds are fickle.
ramayana-2-4-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-21.translation: Today the moon has entered Punarvasu, before Pushya; tomorrow, the astrologers say, it will surely be in Pushya.
ramayana-2-4-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-22.translation: Be crowned at Pushya; my mind urges me on. Tomorrow I will crown you crown prince, scorcher of foes.
ramayana-2-4-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-23.translation: So tonight you and your wife must keep a vow, self-controlled, fasting and sleeping on a bed of darbha grass.
ramayana-2-4-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-24.translation: Let your friends guard you carefully on every side today, for such undertakings meet many obstacles.
ramayana-2-4-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-25.translation: While Bharata is away from the city, I think this is the right time for your coronation.
ramayana-2-4-25.meaning: He wants it done while Bharata is away.
ramayana-2-4-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-26.translation: Certainly your brother Bharata keeps to the conduct of the good, follows his elder, is righteous, compassionate and self-controlled.
ramayana-2-4-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-27.translation: But I believe the minds of men are changeable, Raghava, even of the good who are devoted to dharma.
ramayana-2-4-27.meaning: Yet he worries people can change. Ironically, the danger will come from elsewhere.
ramayana-2-4-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-28.translation: Thus told and dismissed for the coronation set for tomorrow, Rama bowed to his father and went home.
ramayana-2-4-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-29.translation: Entering his house after the king had announced the coronation, he at once went out again to his mother's quarters.
ramayana-2-4-29.meaning: He goes to tell his mother.
ramayana-2-4-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-30.translation: There he saw his mother, devout, in linen, silent in the shrine, praying for his fortune.
ramayana-2-4-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-31.translation: Sumitra and Lakshmana had already come there, and Sita had been brought, hearing the welcome news of Rama's coronation.
ramayana-2-4-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-32.translation: Kausalya stood there with eyes closed, attended by Sumitra, Sita and Lakshmana.
ramayana-2-4-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-33.translation: Having heard of her son's coronation under Pushya, she was meditating on Lord Janardana with breath control.
ramayana-2-4-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-34.translation: Approaching her as she kept her vow, Rama greeted her and, to delight her, said:
ramayana-2-4-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-35.translation: Mother, father has appointed me to protect the people. Tomorrow will be my coronation, as father commands.
ramayana-2-4-35.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-36.translation: Sita too must fast with me tonight; so father told me, with the priests and teachers.
ramayana-2-4-36.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-37.translation: Have whatever blessings are fitting for tomorrow's coronation performed today for me and for Vaidehi.
ramayana-2-4-37.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-38.translation: Hearing what she had long desired, Kausalya spoke to Rama, her voice choked with tears of joy:
ramayana-2-4-38.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-39.translation: Rama, my child, live long; may your foes be destroyed. Gaining royal fortune, bring joy to my kin and Sumitra's.
ramayana-2-4-39.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-40.translation: Surely, my son, you were born to me under a lucky star, since you have won your father Dasharatha by your virtues.
ramayana-2-4-40.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-41.translation: Surely my devotion to the lotus-eyed Lord was not in vain, since this royal fortune of the Ikshvakus will come to you, my son.
ramayana-2-4-41.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-42.translation: Thus addressed by his mother, Rama, looking at his brother seated humbly with folded hands, said with a smile:
ramayana-2-4-42.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-43.translation: Lakshmana, rule this earth with me. You are my second self; this fortune has come to you too.
ramayana-2-4-43.meaning: Rama shares his kingdom with his brother.
ramayana-2-4-43.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-44.translation: Saumitri, enjoy the pleasures you wish and the fruits of kingship. I desire life and kingdom for your sake.
ramayana-2-4-44.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-4-45.translation: Having said this to Lakshmana, Rama bowed to his two mothers, took leave with Sita, and went to his own house.
ramayana-2-4-45.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 4: Troubled by bad omens, Dasharatha decides to crown Rama the very next day, while Bharata is away, and asks Rama and Sita to keep a night of fasting. Rama shares the news with his mother and Lakshmana.

ramayana-2-5-1.translation: Having instructed Rama about tomorrow's coronation, the king summoned his priest Vasishtha and said:
ramayana-2-5-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-2.translation: Go, ascetic, and have Kakutstha and his wife keep the fast today, observing the vow, for fortune, glory and the kingdom.
ramayana-2-5-2.meaning: Vasishtha is to guide the vow.
ramayana-2-5-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-3.translation: Saying So be it, blessed Vasishtha, best of Veda knowers, went himself to Rama's house.
ramayana-2-5-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-4.translation: Reaching Rama's house, bright as a mass of white cloud, the best of sages drove his chariot through three courtyards.
ramayana-2-5-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-5.translation: Seeing the sage arrive, Rama hurried out of the house eagerly to honour him who deserved honour.
ramayana-2-5-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-6.translation: Hurrying to the wise man's chariot, he himself helped him down, holding him.
ramayana-2-5-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-7.translation: Seeing him so humble, the priest spoke with him kindly and, delighting Rama who deserved kindness, said:
ramayana-2-5-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-8.translation: Your father is pleased, Rama; you will become crown prince. Today keep the fast with Sita.
ramayana-2-5-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-9.translation: At dawn your father, King Dasharatha, will lovingly crown you, as Nahusha crowned Yayati.
ramayana-2-5-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-10.translation: Having said this, the sage had Rama, steadfast in his vow, keep the fast with Vaidehi, with proper mantras.
ramayana-2-5-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-11.translation: Then, duly honoured by Rama, the king's teacher took leave of Kakutstha and left Rama's house.
ramayana-2-5-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-12.translation: Rama too, saying goodbye to his friends there and honoured by them, went inside.
ramayana-2-5-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-13.translation: Rama's house, full of joyful men and women, shone like a lake of blooming lotuses with flocks of excited birds.
ramayana-2-5-13.meaning: His house is full of joy.
ramayana-2-5-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-14.translation: Coming out of Rama's palace, which rivalled the king's, Vasishtha saw the road crowded with people.
ramayana-2-5-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-15.translation: On every side in Ayodhya the royal roads were jammed with throngs of curious people.
ramayana-2-5-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-16.translation: The royal road, with waves of crowds jostling and joyful noise, sounded like the ocean.
ramayana-2-5-16.meaning: The city roars like the sea.
ramayana-2-5-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-17.translation: That day the city of Ayodhya, its streets sprinkled and swept, was garlanded with trees, and flags flew high on its houses.
ramayana-2-5-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-18.translation: All the people of Ayodhya, with women, children and the old, longed for Rama's coronation, longing for the sun to rise.
ramayana-2-5-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-19.translation: The people were eager to see that great festival of Ayodhya, the jewel of its people that would increase their joy.
ramayana-2-5-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-20.translation: The priest, as if parting the crowds on the jammed royal road, slowly made his way to the royal palace.
ramayana-2-5-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-21.translation: Climbing the palace, like a white cloud-peak, he met the king as Brihaspati meets Indra.
ramayana-2-5-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-22.translation: Seeing him come, the king rose from his throne and asked; and he told him it was done.
ramayana-2-5-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-23.translation: With his guru's leave, the king dismissed the crowd and entered the inner palace like a lion entering a mountain cave.
ramayana-2-5-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-5-24.translation: The king entered that residence like great Indra's, crowded with finely dressed women, lighting it up, as the moon enters a sky full of stars.
ramayana-2-5-24.meaning: He goes to the queens' quarters, setting the scene for Kaikeyi.
ramayana-2-5-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 5: Vasishtha guides Rama and Sita through the vow of fasting. The whole city fills with excited crowds awaiting the coronation.

ramayana-2-6-1.translation: When the priest had gone, Rama bathed and, with focused mind, approached Narayana with his wide-eyed wife.
ramayana-2-6-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-2.translation: Taking the vessel of offering on his head as prescribed, he offered ghee into the blazing fire to the great deity.
ramayana-2-6-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-3.translation: Eating the rest of the offering and praying for what was dear to him, meditating on Lord Narayana, on a well-spread bed of kusha grass,
ramayana-2-6-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-4.translation: silent with Vaidehi, his mind controlled, the prince slept in the splendid shrine of Vishnu.
ramayana-2-6-4.meaning: They spend the night in the temple.
ramayana-2-6-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-5.translation: Waking when one watch of the night remained, he had the whole house decorated.
ramayana-2-6-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-6.translation: There, hearing the pleasant voices of bards and heralds, he performed the dawn worship and prayed with a controlled mind.
ramayana-2-6-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-7.translation: Bowing his head, he praised Madhusudana and, dressed in clean linen, had brahmins recite blessings.
ramayana-2-6-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-8.translation: Their deep, sweet cries of blessing for a holy day, echoing with music, filled Ayodhya.
ramayana-2-6-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Rama and Sita worship Narayana and spend the night in prayer. At dawn the city resounds with blessings and music.

ramayana-2-6-9.translation: Hearing that Raghava had begun his fast with Vaidehi, all the people of Ayodhya rejoiced.
ramayana-2-6-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-10.translation: Then all the citizens, hearing of Rama's coronation and seeing the night turn to dawn, decorated the city splendidly again.
ramayana-2-6-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-11.translation: On temples like white cloud-peaks, at crossroads and in streets, on sacred trees and watchtowers,
ramayana-2-6-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-12.translation: in merchants' shops full of goods, in the rich, splendid homes of householders,
ramayana-2-6-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-13.translation: in all the halls and on prominent trees, colourful flags and banners were raised.
ramayana-2-6-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-14.translation: Everywhere one heard the voices of actors, dancers and singers, pleasing to mind and ear.
ramayana-2-6-14.meaning: Music and performance fill the streets.
ramayana-2-6-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-15.translation: With the coronation at hand, people talked together about Rama's coronation in squares and homes.
ramayana-2-6-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-16.translation: Even children playing in groups at their doors talked to each other about Rama's coronation.
ramayana-2-6-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-17.translation: For Rama's coronation the citizens made the royal road splendid with offerings of flowers and scented with incense.
ramayana-2-6-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-18.translation: Fearing nightfall, they set up lamp-trees all along the streets to light them.
ramayana-2-6-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-19.translation: Having decorated the city, the citizens, longing for Rama's coronation as crown prince,
ramayana-2-6-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-20.translation: gathered in groups in squares and halls and, talking together, praised the king.
ramayana-2-6-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-21.translation: Ah, this king, joy of the Ikshvakus, is great-souled: knowing himself to be old, he will crown Rama.
ramayana-2-6-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-22.translation: We are all blessed that Rama, who has seen the world's high and low, will long be our king and protector.
ramayana-2-6-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-23.translation: Humble, learned, righteous and loving to his brothers: as Raghava is affectionate to his brothers, so is he to us.
ramayana-2-6-23.meaning: Rama treats the people like family.
ramayana-2-6-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-24.translation: Long live the righteous, sinless King Dasharatha, by whose grace we will see Rama crowned.
ramayana-2-6-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-25.translation: The country people, who had heard the news from every direction, listened to the citizens talking like this.
ramayana-2-6-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-26.translation: Arriving from all directions to see Rama's coronation, the country people filled Rama's city.
ramayana-2-6-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-27.translation: The sound of those surging crowds was heard like the roar of the ocean when its tides rise at the full moon.
ramayana-2-6-27.meaning: The noise is like a tide.
ramayana-2-6-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-6-28.translation: That city, like Indra's home, crowded on all sides with country people come to see, shone loud and teeming like ocean water full of sea creatures.
ramayana-2-6-28.meaning: A vivid picture of the festive crowds.
ramayana-2-6-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 6: Ayodhya is decorated for Rama's coronation, and townsfolk and country people pour in, praising the king and Rama.

ramayana-2-7-1.translation: Kaikeyi's maid, born in her family and brought up with her, happened to climb up to the moon-bright terrace.
ramayana-2-7-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-2.translation: From that terrace Manthara looked out over all Ayodhya, its royal road sprinkled and strewn with lotuses.
ramayana-2-7-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-3.translation: Adorned with fine banners and flags, sprinkled with sandal-water, full of people freshly bathed,
ramayana-2-7-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-4.translation: Seeing a nurse standing nearby, Manthara asked her, the nurse wearing her finest and full of joy:
ramayana-2-7-4.meaning: She asks a nurse what is happening.
ramayana-2-7-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-5.translation: Why is Rama's mother giving wealth to people? Tell me why everyone is so overjoyed. What is the delighted king going to do?
ramayana-2-7-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-6.translation: The nurse, bursting with joy, told the hunchbacked maid of Raghava's great fortune:
ramayana-2-7-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-7.translation: Tomorrow under Pushya King Dasharatha will crown sinless Rama, who has conquered anger, as crown prince.
ramayana-2-7-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-8.translation: Hearing the nurse, the maid, instantly resentful, came down from the palace shaped like a Kailasa peak.
ramayana-2-7-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-9.translation: Burning with anger, evil-minded Manthara went to Kaikeyi as she lay resting and said:
ramayana-2-7-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-10.translation: Get up, foolish woman! How can you lie there when danger threatens you? Don't you see you are swamped by a great flood?
ramayana-2-7-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-11.translation: Unlucky one with the look of a lucky one, you boast of your good fortune; but your fortune is fleeting, like a river's flow in summer.
ramayana-2-7-11.meaning: She says Kaikeyi's favour will dry up.
ramayana-2-7-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-12.translation: Told these harsh words by the angry, evil-minded maid, Kaikeyi was deeply troubled.
ramayana-2-7-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-13.translation: Kaikeyi said to her: Is something wrong, Manthara? I see your face is sad and you are very upset.
ramayana-2-7-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-14.translation: Hearing Kaikeyi's sweet words, Manthara, clever with words, answered angrily.
ramayana-2-7-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-15.translation: More dejected still, the maid, appearing to seek her good, spoke to dismay her and to turn her against Raghava:
ramayana-2-7-15.meaning: She sets out to divide them.
ramayana-2-7-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-16.translation: A great disaster has begun, queen, that will ruin you: King Dasharatha will crown Rama as crown prince.
ramayana-2-7-16.meaning: She presents Rama's rise as a threat.
ramayana-2-7-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-17.translation: I am sunk in bottomless fear, full of grief, burning as if in fire; I have come here for your sake.
ramayana-2-7-17.meaning: She claims to act out of loyalty.
ramayana-2-7-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-18.translation: Your sorrow would be my great sorrow, Kaikeyi, and your rise my rise; of this there is no doubt.
ramayana-2-7-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-19.translation: You were born in a royal family and are the king's queen; how can you not understand how harsh royal politics is?
ramayana-2-7-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-20.translation: Your husband talks of dharma but is deceitful; he speaks softly but is cruel. Pure-hearted, you do not see it, so you have been tricked.
ramayana-2-7-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.

ramayana-2-7-21.translation: Your husband offers you empty comfort, while he will give real benefit to Kausalya today.
ramayana-2-7-21.meaning: She says the king favours Kausalya.
ramayana-2-7-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 7: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, sees the celebrations and urges Kaikeyi that Rama's rise means her ruin. At first Kaikeyi is delighted for Rama and rewards her.
