ramayana-2-28-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-17.translation: Self-possessed Rama lovingly said to Lakshmana: You have come at the time I wished, gentle Lakshmana.
ramayana-2-28-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-18.translation: I want to give away this wealth of mine to brahmins and ascetics with you, tamer of foes.
ramayana-2-28-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-19.translation: The best of brahmins who live here with firm devotion to our elders, and all my dependants too,
ramayana-2-28-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-20.translation: bring quickly noble Suyajna, son of Vasishtha, best of brahmins. I will go to the forest after honouring him and all the other learned brahmins.
ramayana-2-28-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-29-1.translation: Understanding his brother's kind and welcome command, he went and quickly entered Suyajna's house.
ramayana-2-29-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-2.translation: Bowing to the brahmin in his fire-room, Lakshmana said: Friend, come and see the house of one doing a hard thing.
ramayana-2-29-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-3.translation: After the evening prayer he quickly went with Saumitri and entered Rama's lovely, splendid house.
ramayana-2-29-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-4.translation: Raghava with Sita came forward with folded hands to the learned Suyajna, as to a worshipped fire.
ramayana-2-29-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-5.translation: With fine gold armlets, lovely earrings, gold threads with gems, bracelets and bangles,
ramayana-2-29-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-6.translation: and many other jewels Kakutstha honoured him, and Rama, urged by Sita, said to Suyajna:
ramayana-2-29-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-7.translation: Take this necklace and gold chain for your wife, gentle one; and Sita wants to give you her girdle now, friend.
ramayana-2-29-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-8.translation: Vaidehi also wants to give you this couch with a fine cover, adorned with many jewels.
ramayana-2-29-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-9.translation: The elephant named Shatrunjaya that my uncle gave me, I give you with a thousand elephants, best of brahmins.
ramayana-2-29-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-10.translation: Thus addressed by Rama, Suyajna accepted it and gave auspicious blessings to Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.
ramayana-2-29-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-11.translation: Then kind-spoken Rama said to his calm, dear brother Saumitri, as Brahma speaks to Indra:
ramayana-2-29-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-12.translation: Invite and honour with jewels the two best of brahmins, Agastya and Kaushika, as crops are refreshed with rain.
ramayana-2-29-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-13.translation: The devoted teacher of the Taittiriya school, handsome and learned, who serves Kausalya with blessings,
ramayana-2-29-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-14.translation: give him a carriage, servant women and silk clothes until that brahmin is satisfied, Saumitri.
ramayana-2-29-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-15.translation: And noble Chitraratha, the charioteer and long-serving counsellor, please him with costly jewels, clothes and wealth.
ramayana-2-29-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-16.translation: And a thousand loads of rice, two hundred oxen and, for dairy, a thousand cows, Saumitri.
ramayana-2-29-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-17.translation: Then Lakshmana, tiger among men, himself gave that wealth to the best brahmins as instructed, like Kubera.
ramayana-2-29-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-18.translation: Then he spoke to the dependants standing there, choked with tears, having given much to each one:
ramayana-2-29-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-19.translation: Keep Lakshmana's house and this home of mine each occupied until I return.
ramayana-2-29-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-20.translation: Having said this to all those grieving dependants, he told the treasurer: Bring the wealth. And the dependants brought all his wealth.
ramayana-2-29-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-21.translation: Then the tiger among men with Lakshmana had it given to brahmins, children, the old and the poor.
ramayana-2-29-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-22.translation: There was a brahmin there named Trijata of the Garga clan, tawny-haired; no one stopped him up to the fifth courtyard.
ramayana-2-29-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-23.translation: Reaching the prince, Trijata said: I am poor with many sons, famous prince. I live by gleaning in the forest; look after me.
ramayana-2-29-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-24.translation: Rama, in a playful mood, said to him: I have not yet given away even one thousand cows. As far as you can throw your staff, you will get that many.
ramayana-2-29-24.meaning: A gentle joke and a generous offer.
ramayana-2-29-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-25.translation: He quickly, eagerly tied his cloth round his waist, whirled his staff and threw it with all his strength.
ramayana-2-29-25.meaning: Trijata throws with all his might.
ramayana-2-29-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-26.translation: Then Rama, comforting that Garga, said: Do not be offended; this was just my joke.
ramayana-2-29-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-27.translation: Then the great sage Trijata with his wife, receiving a herd of cows, delighted, gave great Rama blessings that increase fame, strength, love and happiness.
ramayana-2-29-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-30-1.translation: Having given much wealth to brahmins with Vaidehi, the two Raghavas went with Sita to see their father.
ramayana-2-30-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-2.translation: The weapons they carried, hard to look at, shone, hung with garlands and adorned by Sita.
ramayana-2-30-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-3.translation: Then the people climbed palaces, mansions and towers and watched sorrowfully.
ramayana-2-30-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-4.translation: The streets were too crowded to walk, so they climbed the palaces and gazed sadly at Raghava.
ramayana-2-30-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-5.translation: Seeing Rama on foot, without his umbrella, the people, stricken with grief, said many things.
ramayana-2-30-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-6.translation: He whom a great four-part army used to follow is followed now only by Lakshmana with Sita.
ramayana-2-30-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-7.translation: Though he knows the taste of power and grants desires, he will not make his father a liar, out of reverence for dharma.
ramayana-2-30-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-8.translation: Sita, whom even beings in the sky could not see before, the people on the royal road see today.
ramayana-2-30-8.meaning: Sita is seen in public for the first time.
ramayana-2-30-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-9.translation: Sita, used to cosmetics and red sandal paste, will soon be darkened by rain, heat and cold.
ramayana-2-30-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-10.translation: Surely Dasharatha speaks today possessed by some spirit; no king would banish his dear son.
ramayana-2-30-10.meaning: They think the king is not himself.
ramayana-2-30-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-11.translation: How could even a worthless son be banished? How much more one who has won this world by his conduct alone?
ramayana-2-30-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-12.translation: Kindness, compassion, learning, character, self-control and calm: these six virtues adorn Raghava, best of men.
ramayana-2-30-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-13.translation: So the people are deeply pained by his injury, like water creatures when the water dries up in summer.
ramayana-2-30-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-14.translation: The whole world is pained by the pain of this lord of the world, as a flowering, fruiting tree is when its root is cut.
ramayana-2-30-14.meaning: Rama is the root of their happiness.
ramayana-2-30-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-15.translation: Like Lakshmana, let us quickly follow where Raghava goes, with our wives and kin.
ramayana-2-30-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-16.translation: Leaving gardens, fields and homes, sharing one sorrow and joy, let us follow righteous Rama.
ramayana-2-30-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-17.translation: Let Kaikeyi take our abandoned houses, their treasure dug up, courtyards ruined, grain and wealth removed, stripped of all value,
ramayana-2-30-17.meaning: They will leave the city empty.
ramayana-2-30-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-18.translation: covered in dust, deserted by the household gods, abandoned by us.
ramayana-2-30-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-19.translation: Let the forest where Raghava goes become a city, and let the city we abandon become a forest.
ramayana-2-30-19.meaning: The people go where Rama goes.
ramayana-2-30-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-20.translation: Let fanged beasts leave their dens, and deer and birds their slopes, and come to live in what we abandon.
ramayana-2-30-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-21.translation: Rama heard these many things said by all kinds of people, and hearing them, his mind did not change.
ramayana-2-30-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-22.translation: Looking at the distressed people, himself showing no distress, almost smiling, Rama went to see his father, wishing to do his command properly.
ramayana-2-30-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-23.translation: Before going, great Rama, Ikshvaku's son, about to leave for the forest, stood seeing Sumantra stricken, waiting to be announced to his father.
ramayana-2-30-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-24.translation: Devoted to dharma, resolved to enter the forest by his father's command, Raghava, seeing Sumantra, said: Announce my coming to the king.
ramayana-2-30-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-31-1.translation: Sent by Rama, the charioteer, his senses clouded by grief, went in quickly and saw the king sighing.
ramayana-2-31-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-2.translation: Seeing the king deeply troubled, grieving for Rama, the wise charioteer approached him with folded hands.
ramayana-2-31-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-3.translation: Here is your son at the door, tiger among men, having given all his wealth to brahmins and dependants.
ramayana-2-31-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-4.translation: Let Rama, true in valour, see you, bless you. Having taken leave of all his friends, he wishes to see you now.
ramayana-2-31-4.meaning: He has said goodbye to everyone.
ramayana-2-31-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-5.translation: He will go to the great forest; see him, lord of the earth, endowed with every kingly virtue like the sun with its rays.
ramayana-2-31-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-6.translation: The truthful, righteous king, deep as the ocean and clear as the sky, replied:
ramayana-2-31-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-7.translation: Sumantra, bring all my wives who are here; I want to see Raghava surrounded by all my wives.
ramayana-2-31-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-8.translation: Going into the inner palace he said to the women: The noble king calls you; go there without delay.
ramayana-2-31-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-9.translation: Thus told by Sumantra at the king's command, all the women went to that hall, knowing their husband's order.
ramayana-2-31-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-10.translation: Three hundred and fifty women with red-rimmed eyes, keeping their vows, slowly came surrounding Kausalya.
ramayana-2-31-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-11.translation: When the wives had come, the lord of the earth, seeing them, said to the charioteer: Sumantra, bring my son.
ramayana-2-31-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-12.translation: The charioteer, bringing Rama, Lakshmana and Maithili, went quickly towards the lord of the earth.
ramayana-2-31-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-13.translation: The king, seeing his son coming from afar with folded hands, sprang up from his seat, distressed, surrounded by the women.
ramayana-2-31-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-14.translation: The lord of people ran fast towards Rama, but before reaching him, stricken with grief, fell fainting to the ground.
ramayana-2-31-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-15.translation: Rama and the great warrior Lakshmana quickly rushed to the king, unconscious with grief and sorrow.
ramayana-2-31-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-16.translation: A cry of a thousand women rose in the palace, Alas, Rama! mixed with the sound of their ornaments.
ramayana-2-31-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-17.translation: Embracing him with their arms, Rama and Lakshmana with Sita, weeping, laid him on the couch.
ramayana-2-31-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-18.translation: After a while, when the king regained consciousness, Rama, with folded hands, spoke to him, drowning in an ocean of grief:
ramayana-2-31-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-19.translation: I take leave of you, great king; you are lord of us all. See me safely off to the Dandaka forest.
ramayana-2-31-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-20.translation: Give Lakshmana leave too, and Sita follows me to the forest; though held back with many true reasons, they will not stay.
ramayana-2-31-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-21.translation: Give us all leave, giver of honour, setting grief aside, Lakshmana, me and Sita, as the Creator does his creatures.
ramayana-2-31-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-22.translation: Seeing Raghava calmly waiting for his permission to live in the forest, the king said:
ramayana-2-31-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-23.translation: Raghava, I am deluded by the boon I gave Kaikeyi. Restrain me and become king of Ayodhya yourself today.
ramayana-2-31-23.meaning: He urges Rama to overthrow him.
ramayana-2-31-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-24.translation: Thus addressed by the king, Rama, best of upholders of dharma, skilled in speech, folded his hands and replied:
ramayana-2-31-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-25.translation: May you be lord of the earth for a thousand years, O king. I will live in the forest; I must not make you a liar.
ramayana-2-31-25.meaning: He will not let his father break his word.
ramayana-2-31-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-26.translation: Go, my son, for good fortune, growth and return, on a safe path, untroubled and free of fear from any side.
ramayana-2-31-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-27.translation: But do not go now tonight, son, in any case. Seeing your mother and me, stay this one night; satisfied with all you want, you can set out tomorrow.
ramayana-2-31-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-28.translation: Hearing the words of his grieving father, Rama, sad, with his brother Lakshmana, said:
ramayana-2-31-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-29.translation: Who will give me tomorrow the good things I would get today? So I choose leaving over all desires.
ramayana-2-31-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-30.translation: Let this earth, with its kingdom and people, full of wealth and grain, which I give up, be given to Bharata.
ramayana-2-31-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-31.translation: Let your sorrow go; do not be drowned in tears. The invincible ocean, lord of rivers, is not shaken.
ramayana-2-31-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-32.translation: I want neither kingdom, nor happiness, nor even Maithili; I want you to be truthful, not false, bull among men.
ramayana-2-31-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-33.translation: Let the city, the kingdom and the whole earth I give up be given to Bharata. Keeping your command, I will go to the forest to live there a long time.
ramayana-2-31-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-34.translation: Let Bharata alone rule this earth I give up, with its mountains, cities and forests, auspicious and well bounded; let what you said be so, O king.
ramayana-2-31-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-35.translation: My mind is not set so much on great pleasures or on what is dear to me as on your command approved by the good. Let your sorrow on my account pass, sinless one.
ramayana-2-31-35.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-36.translation: So today, sinless one, I would not choose the lasting kingdom, nor all pleasures, nor happiness, nor Maithili, nor life, by making you false. Let your vow be true.
ramayana-2-31-36.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-31-37.translation: Eating fruits and roots in the forest, seeing mountains, rivers and lakes, entering the forest of many trees, I will be happy. Be at peace.
ramayana-2-31-37.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Rama takes leave of his father. Dasharatha begs him to seize the throne or at least stay one more night; Rama gently refuses, choosing truth over kingdom, comfort and even Sita.

ramayana-2-32-1.translation: Then the Ikshvaku king, tormented by his promise, sighing deeply with tears, said to Sumantra again and again:
ramayana-2-32-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-2.translation: Charioteer, quickly prepare a four-part army full of treasure to follow Raghava.
ramayana-2-32-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-3.translation: Let courtesans, skilled women and wealthy merchants adorn the prince's train, spread out widely.
ramayana-2-32-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-4.translation: Those who live by him and those whose prowess he enjoys, give them many things and assign them here too.
ramayana-2-32-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-5.translation: Killing deer and elephants, drinking forest honey, seeing many rivers, he will not remember the kingdom.
ramayana-2-32-5.meaning: He wants Rama to live comfortably.
ramayana-2-32-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-6.translation: Let whatever granary and treasury of mine follow Rama as he lives in the lonely forest.
ramayana-2-32-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-7.translation: Sacrificing in holy places and giving generous fees, meeting with sages, he will live happily in the forest.
ramayana-2-32-7.meaning: He hopes Rama's life will be rich.
ramayana-2-32-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-8.translation: Mighty Bharata will protect Ayodhya; let glorious Rama be provided with every desire.
ramayana-2-32-8.meaning: Bharata will rule; Rama will lack nothing.
ramayana-2-32-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-9.translation: As Kakutstha spoke, fear came over Kaikeyi; her mouth went dry and her voice was choked.
ramayana-2-32-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-10.translation: Dismayed and frightened, Kaikeyi said: Good sir, Bharata will not accept a kingdom emptied of people, like wine with its essence drunk, utterly tasteless and void.
ramayana-2-32-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-11.translation: As Kaikeyi, shameless, spoke so very cruelly, King Dasharatha said to the wide-eyed woman: Why do you goad me when I carry the burden you placed on me?
ramayana-2-32-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-12.translation: Kaikeyi, twice as angry, said to the king: In your own line Sagara banished his eldest son, known as Asamanja; so this one should go.
ramayana-2-32-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-13.translation: Thus addressed, King Dasharatha said only, Shame! All the people were ashamed, but she did not understand.
ramayana-2-32-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-14.translation: There an old chief minister named Siddhartha, honest and esteemed by the king, said to Kaikeyi:
ramayana-2-32-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-15.translation: Asamanja used to seize children on the road in play and throw them into the waters of the Sarayu; the wicked one enjoyed it.
ramayana-2-32-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-16.translation: Seeing that, all the citizens angrily told the king: Choose Asamanja alone, or us, you who prosper the kingdom.
ramayana-2-32-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-17.translation: The king asked them: Why this fear? Asked by the king, the people said:
ramayana-2-32-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-18.translation: He, out of his mind, seizes our little sons in play and throws them into the Sarayu, and in his folly takes great delight in it.
ramayana-2-32-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-19.translation: Hearing the people, O king, he cast off that harmful son to please them.
ramayana-2-32-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-20.translation: So righteous King Sagara cast him off. What wrong has Rama done to be banished like this?
ramayana-2-32-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-21.translation: Hearing Siddhartha, the king, his voice weaker still, said to Kaikeyi in a grief-stricken voice:
ramayana-2-32-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-32-22.translation: I will follow Rama today, giving up kingdom, comfort and wealth. You, with King Bharata, enjoy the kingdom as you please for a long time.
ramayana-2-32-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 32: Dasharatha orders an army and treasury to go with Rama. Kaikeyi objects; the old minister Siddhartha rebukes her, and the king says he will follow Rama himself.

ramayana-2-33-1.translation: Hearing the chief minister, Rama, knowing humility, humbly spoke to Dasharatha:
ramayana-2-33-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-2.translation: I have given up pleasures and will live on forest food, O king. What use is a following to me, who have given up all attachments?
ramayana-2-33-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-3.translation: Who, having given away the best elephant, sets his heart on the girth rope? What is the rope to one giving up the elephant?
ramayana-2-33-3.meaning: Why keep small things after giving up the kingdom?
ramayana-2-33-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-4.translation: So, best of the good, what use is an army to me, lord of the world? I give up everything. Let them bring me just bark garments.
ramayana-2-33-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-5.translation: Bring me a spade and a basket as I go, to live fourteen years in the forest.
ramayana-2-33-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-6.translation: Then Kaikeyi herself brought bark garments to Raghava and said shamelessly before the crowd, Put them on.
ramayana-2-33-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-7.translation: Taking the bark garments from Kaikeyi, the tiger among men threw off his fine clothes and put on a sage's dress.
ramayana-2-33-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-8.translation: Lakshmana too, right there before his father, left his fine clothes and took the ascetic's dress.
ramayana-2-33-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-9.translation: Then Sita, dressed in silk, seeing the bark garment meant for her, shrank like a doe from a net.
ramayana-2-33-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-10.translation: Taking it, ashamed and unhappy, she said to her husband, handsome as a gandharva king: How do forest sages tie their bark garments?
ramayana-2-33-10.meaning: She does not know how to wear it.
ramayana-2-33-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-11.translation: Putting one around her neck and holding one in her hand, Janaka's daughter stood there, clumsy and embarrassed.
ramayana-2-33-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-12.translation: Rama, best of upholders of dharma, came quickly and himself tied the bark garment over her silk.
ramayana-2-33-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-13.translation: Seeing her, who had a protector, wearing bark as if she had none, all the people cried out: Shame on you, Dasharatha!
ramayana-2-33-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-14.translation: Sighing hot, the Ikshvaku said to his wife: Kaikeyi, Sita should not go in a bark garment.
ramayana-2-33-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-15.translation: Surely Rama's banishment is enough for you, wicked one. Why add these mean sins?
ramayana-2-33-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-16.translation: To his father speaking so, sitting with bowed head, Rama, setting out for the forest, said:
ramayana-2-33-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-17.translation: Righteous one, this Kausalya is my famous mother, old and of noble character; she does not blame you, lord of gods.
ramayana-2-33-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-18.translation: Without me, giver of boons, sunk in an ocean of grief, never having known misfortune, she deserves your greater respect.
ramayana-2-33-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-33-19.translation: Treat my mother, who bore a son like great Indra, so that, worn by grief while I am in the forest, she does not give up her life and go to Yama's realm.
ramayana-2-33-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 33: Rama refuses the army and asks only for bark garments. Kaikeyi hands them over; Sita does not know how to wear them, and Rama ties one over her silk. The crowd curses the king.

ramayana-2-34-1.translation: Hearing Rama's words and seeing him in a sage's dress, the king with his wives lost consciousness.
ramayana-2-34-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-2.translation: Burning with sorrow, he could not look at Raghava, nor, seeing him, speak to him in his misery.
ramayana-2-34-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-3.translation: For a while the king lay unconscious and grieving; then the mighty-armed one lamented, thinking only of Rama.
ramayana-2-34-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-4.translation: I think I must have separated many cows from their calves before, or harmed living things; that is why this has come.
ramayana-2-34-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-5.translation: Life does not leave the body before its time; though tormented by Kaikeyi, I do not die.
ramayana-2-34-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-6.translation: I see before me my son, bright as fire, having put off fine clothes for an ascetic's covering.
ramayana-2-34-6.meaning: Seeing Rama in bark pains him.
ramayana-2-34-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-7.translation: Because of one woman, Kaikeyi, these people suffer; she strives for her own ends, relying on this deceit.
ramayana-2-34-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-8.translation: Saying this, his eyes veiled with tears, he said Rama only once and could speak no more.
ramayana-2-34-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-9.translation: Regaining consciousness after a while, the king, his eyes full of tears, said to Sumantra:
ramayana-2-34-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-10.translation: Yoke the riding chariot with the best horses and come; take this fortunate one beyond this country.
ramayana-2-34-10.meaning: Drive Rama out of the kingdom.
ramayana-2-34-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-11.translation: This, I think, is called the fruit of virtue in the virtuous: that a good and heroic son is banished to the forest by his father and mother.
ramayana-2-34-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-12.translation: Understanding the king's command, swift Sumantra yoked and brought the chariot with decorated horses.
ramayana-2-34-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-13.translation: With folded hands the charioteer told the prince the gold-adorned chariot was yoked to the finest horses.
ramayana-2-34-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-14.translation: The king quickly called the treasurer, who knew place and time, was resolute and honest in every way, and said:
ramayana-2-34-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-15.translation: Counting these years, quickly bring costly clothes and fine ornaments for Vaidehi.
ramayana-2-34-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-16.translation: Thus told by the king, he went to the treasury and quickly brought everything and gave it to Sita.
ramayana-2-34-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-17.translation: Noble Vaidehi, setting out for the forest, adorned her limbs with those lovely, varied ornaments.
ramayana-2-34-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-18.translation: Well adorned, Vaidehi lit up the palace, as the radiance of the rising sun lights the sky.
ramayana-2-34-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-19.translation: Her mother-in-law embraced her with both arms, kissed Maithili on the head, who never acted meanly, and said:
ramayana-2-34-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-20.translation: In this whole world, unfaithful women, though always honoured by loved ones, do not respect a husband fallen on misfortune.
ramayana-2-34-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-21.translation: Do not slight my banished son. Let him be your god, poor or rich.
ramayana-2-34-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-22.translation: Understanding her words full of dharma and purpose, Sita stood before her mother-in-law with folded hands and said:
ramayana-2-34-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-23.translation: I will do everything the noble lady teaches me. I know how to behave towards my husband; I have heard it.
ramayana-2-34-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-24.translation: The noble lady should not compare me with bad women; I cannot swerve from dharma, as light cannot leave the moon.
ramayana-2-34-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-25.translation: A vina does not play without strings, a chariot does not run without wheels; a woman without her husband does not thrive in happiness, even with a hundred sons.
ramayana-2-34-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-26.translation: Father gives in measure, mother gives in measure, son gives in measure; what woman would not honour her husband, giver of what cannot be measured?
ramayana-2-34-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-27.translation: Being such, and having heard what is higher and lower in dharma, noble lady, how could I slight him? For women, the husband is a god.
ramayana-2-34-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: The grieving king orders a chariot and fine clothes and jewels for Sita. Kausalya counsels Sita on loyalty; Sita answers that a husband is beyond price. Context: the epic's ideals of marriage are presented as the text states them.

ramayana-2-34-28.translation: Hearing Sita's heartfelt words, pure-hearted Kausalya suddenly shed tears born of both sorrow and joy.
ramayana-2-34-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-29.translation: Approaching with folded hands his mother, highly honoured among the mothers, Rama, who knew dharma well, said:
ramayana-2-34-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-30.translation: Mother, do not grieve; look after my father. The end of the forest exile will come quickly.
ramayana-2-34-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-31.translation: Nine and five years will pass as if you slept. You will see me back here whole, surrounded by friends.
ramayana-2-34-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-32.translation: Having said these meaningful words to his mother, he looked round and saw the three hundred and fifty mothers.
ramayana-2-34-32.meaning: He sees his father's other wives.
ramayana-2-34-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-33.translation: To those mothers, equally grieved, Dasharatha's son spoke these words full of dharma with folded hands:
ramayana-2-34-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-34.translation: Whatever harshness I may have done through living together or unknowingly, forgive me; I take leave of you all.
ramayana-2-34-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-35.translation: As Raghava spoke, the wives of the lord of men cried out like curlews.
ramayana-2-34-35.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-34-36.translation: Dasharatha's palace, once resounding like drums and thunder, was now filled with laments and cries, stricken with disaster.
ramayana-2-34-36.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 34: Rama comforts his mother and asks forgiveness of all his father's queens.

ramayana-2-35-1.translation: Then Rama, Sita and Lakshmana, with folded hands, touched the king's feet and sadly walked round him.
ramayana-2-35-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-2.translation: Taking leave of him, righteous Raghava with Sita, bewildered with grief, saluted his mother.
ramayana-2-35-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-3.translation: Right after his brother, Lakshmana saluted Kausalya, and then clasped the feet of his own mother Sumitra.
ramayana-2-35-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-4.translation: As he bowed, his weeping mother, wishing him well, kissed mighty-armed Lakshmana on the head and said:
ramayana-2-35-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-5.translation: You are sent to live in the forest, devoted to your loved one. Do not be careless about Rama, son, as your brother goes.
ramayana-2-35-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-6.translation: In misfortune or prosperity he is your refuge, sinless one. This is the dharma of the good in the world, to obey the eldest.
ramayana-2-35-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-7.translation: This is the eternal, fitting conduct of this family: giving, consecration in sacrifices, and giving one's body in battle.
ramayana-2-35-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-8.translation: Know Rama as Dasharatha, know Janaka's daughter as me, know the forest as Ayodhya. Go, my son, happily.
ramayana-2-35-8.meaning: Famous blessing: treat Rama as father, Sita as mother, the forest as home.
ramayana-2-35-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-9.translation: Then Sumantra, humble and knowing courtesy, spoke to Kakutstha with folded hands, as Matali speaks to Indra:
ramayana-2-35-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-10.translation: Mount the chariot, bless you, famous prince. I will quickly take you wherever you tell me, Rama.
ramayana-2-35-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-11.translation: You must live fourteen years in the forest; they must begin, as the queen has urged.
ramayana-2-35-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-12.translation: Lovely Sita, having adorned herself, mounted that sun-bright chariot with a glad heart.
ramayana-2-35-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-13.translation: Placing the brothers' weapons and armour in the chariot, along with the leather-covered basket,
ramayana-2-35-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-14.translation: seeing the three mounted with Sita, Sumantra boldly urged on the fine horses, swift as the wind.
ramayana-2-35-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-15.translation: As Raghava left for the great forest for so long, the city fainted, and the army and people fainted too.
ramayana-2-35-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-16.translation: The city was in uproar and confusion, with maddened, angry elephants and the neighing and jingling of horses.
ramayana-2-35-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-17.translation: Then the whole city, children and old, deeply pained, ran after Rama like the heat-struck to water.
ramayana-2-35-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-18.translation: Hanging on at the sides and behind, looking up at him, their faces full of tears, all said in deep sorrow:
ramayana-2-35-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-19.translation: Hold the horses' reins, charioteer; go slowly, slowly. We want to see Rama's face; soon it will be hard to see.
ramayana-2-35-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-20.translation: Surely Rama's mother has a heart of iron, since it does not break as her god-like son goes to the forest.
ramayana-2-35-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-21.translation: Vaidehi has done her duty, following her husband like a shadow; devoted to dharma, she does not leave him, as sunlight does not leave Meru.
ramayana-2-35-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-22.translation: Ah, Lakshmana, you have succeeded, for you will serve your god-like, ever kind-spoken brother.
ramayana-2-35-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-23.translation: This is a great achievement for you, a great rise, the road to heaven, that you follow him. Saying this, they could not hold back their tears.
ramayana-2-35-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-24.translation: Then the king, surrounded by his grieving wives, came out of the palace saying, I will see my dear son.
ramayana-2-35-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-25.translation: Ahead was heard a great cry of weeping women, like the cries of cow-elephants when a great bull elephant is bound.
ramayana-2-35-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-26.translation: Glorious King Kakutstha, the father, looked sunk, like the full moon eclipsed.
ramayana-2-35-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-27.translation: Then a tumult rose behind Rama, as the men saw the king sinking in deep sorrow.
ramayana-2-35-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-28.translation: Some cried, Ah Rama! others, Ah Rama's mother! and they mourned the wailing inner palace.
ramayana-2-35-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-29.translation: Looking back, Rama saw the king and his mother, dejected and confused, following on the road; bound by the noose of dharma, he did not look at them openly.
ramayana-2-35-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-30.translation: Seeing them on foot, who deserved carriages, unused to sorrow and used to comfort, he urged the charioteer, Go quickly.
ramayana-2-35-30.meaning: He hurries away to spare them.
ramayana-2-35-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-31.translation: The tiger among men could not bear the painful sight of his father and mother, like an elephant goaded by a spike.
ramayana-2-35-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-32.translation: He looked again and again at Kausalya running after the chariot, weeping, crying Rama, Rama! Ah Sita, Lakshmana! as if she were dancing.
ramayana-2-35-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-33.translation: Stop! cried the king. Go, go! said Raghava. Sumantra's mind was as if caught between two wheels.
ramayana-2-35-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-34.translation: Even if reproached by the king, you can say, I did not hear. Long grief is worst of all, Rama told him.
ramayana-2-35-34.meaning: Rama asks him to drive on.
ramayana-2-35-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-35.translation: Doing Rama's word and taking leave of the people, the charioteer urged the already moving horses faster.
ramayana-2-35-35.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-36.translation: The king's people walked round Rama and turned back, but in mind and tears they did not turn back.
ramayana-2-35-36.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-37.translation: One should not follow far someone one wishes to return, the ministers told great King Dasharatha.
ramayana-2-35-37.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-35-38.translation: Hearing their wise words, the wretched king with his wives, sweating and dejected, stood looking at his son.
ramayana-2-35-38.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 35: Sumitra blesses Lakshmana: treat Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya. The three leave by chariot as the city wails; Dasharatha and Kausalya run after them.

ramayana-2-36-1.translation: As that tiger among men left with folded hands, a great cry of distress rose among the women of the palace.
ramayana-2-36-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-2.translation: Where is he going, the protector who was the refuge and shelter of these helpless, weak, suffering people?
ramayana-2-36-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-3.translation: He did not get angry even when insulted, avoided what causes anger, soothed all who were angry and shared their sorrow; where is he going?
ramayana-2-36-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-4.translation: He treated us as he treated his own mother Kausalya; where is that great soul going?
ramayana-2-36-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-5.translation: Driven to the forest by the king, tormented by Kaikeyi, where is the saviour of these people and of the world going?
ramayana-2-36-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-6.translation: Ah, the king is senseless: Rama, beloved of the living world, righteous and true to his vows, will live in the forest!
ramayana-2-36-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-7.translation: So all those queens wept like cows bereft of their calves and cried aloud in sorrow.
ramayana-2-36-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-8.translation: Hearing that terrible cry of grief in the inner palace, the king, burning with grief for his son, was deeply pained.
ramayana-2-36-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-9.translation: The fire offerings were not made, the sun disappeared, elephants dropped their food and cows did not suckle their calves.
ramayana-2-36-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-10.translation: Trishanku, Mars, Jupiter and Mercury, fierce planets, all stood near the moon.
ramayana-2-36-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-11.translation: The stars lost their light and the planets their brightness; the Vishakha stars shone in the sky as if in smoke.
ramayana-2-36-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-12.translation: Suddenly all the townspeople fell into misery; no one set his mind on eating or pleasure.
ramayana-2-36-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-13.translation: People on the royal road had tear-stained faces; no one looked happy; all were sunk in grief.
ramayana-2-36-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-14.translation: No cool wind blew, the moon looked unkind, the sun did not warm the world; the whole world was in turmoil.
ramayana-2-36-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 36: The palace and city mourn. Omens darken the sky and no one eats, plays or works.

ramayana-2-36-15.translation: Sons, women, husbands and brothers lost interest in each other; leaving everything, they thought only of Rama.
ramayana-2-36-15.meaning: Only Rama is on their minds.
